transcript:
Header: 2025-11-05 15:00 UTC | Duration: 38m
Attendees: Ellen Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Li (Redwood SE), Priya Desai (OrionFin CTO), Miguel Santos (Platform Eng), Leah Kim (Security)
Links shared: Redwood quickstart deck (shortlink: https://redwood.ai/qs-orionfin), preliminary sizing sheet (sent after call), SOC2 snapshot (customer requested)

Summary: Short discovery focused on time-to-first-token for PLG/self-serve, clarifying hosted vs dedicated/private tradeoffs, security/compliance needs (VPC, KMS), and next steps to run a quick first-token benchmark during proof-of-concept.

Topics: quickstart flow, free credits, SDK install, API keys, time-to-first-token, hosted vs dedicated vs private, data residency, SOC2/KMS/SSO, expected throughput and cost, sample configs for autoscaling and KV cache.

Transcript:
00:00 Ellen Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Ellen from Redwood, AE on the account. Marcus from SE will run through the quickstart and then we'll get into hosting options. How's everyone doing?
00:07 Priya Desai: Good thanks, Priya here. High-level, we're evaluating options to add LLM features to our payments reconciliation flow. Biggest constraints are latency under 500ms for short prompts, cost per 1k tokens, and SOC2 compliance.
00:22 Ellen Park: Great, understood. Quick question, do you plan to start with our hosted API (self-serve) or are you already looking at Dedicated or Private from day one?
00:29 Miguel Santos: We want to prototype quickly with hosted to get time-to-first-token low, but infra wants to know what Dedicated or VPC-hosted would look like if we go to production.
00:38 Marcus Li: Perfect, that's a pretty common path. For self-serve hosted you can be up in minutes — SDK install, API key, curl example — we typically see teams get a first token in less than 10 minutes, often 2-5 if you have a code sample.
00:54 Leah Kim: Can you spell that out? We need to show security to our compliance team. For hosted, are logs accessible, and what controls do you have for key rotation, KMS, HSM?
01:02 Ellen Park: Yep. Hosted comes with RBAC, token rotation in the console, and we integrate with customer KMS for Private deployments. For Hosted we store logs for a default retention window but we can configure retention length or opt for no-log ingest for certain routes. We'll share the security whitepaper.
01:21 Miguel Santos: And VPC/private means we'd have the control plane still with Redwood but the runtime in our VPC? We're curious about traffic egress.
01:29 Marcus Li: Two flavours — Redwood Private (VPC peered control plane + runtime in your VPC) or on-prem package. For VPC deployments traffic stays in your network — you control gradients with KMS, and there's an option for mTLS and HSM integration. There's some setup but it's the usual infra work.
01:45 Priya Desai: On the cost front — what's the ballpark delta between hosted and dedicated? We're trying to model cost per 1M tokens for our reckoning microservice.
01:54 Ellen Park: Ballpark: hosted gives you convenience and elastic capacity, dedicated lowers unit costs at committed volumes — roughly 20-40% savings at scale depending on model and quantization. We'll send a sample costing sheet. Remember batching and KV cache reduce per-token cost too.
02:12 Miguel Santos: You mentioned KV cache — how transparent is that? We have lots of similar prefixes in reconciliation prompts.
02:18 Marcus Li: The runtime does prefix/KV caching automatically for repeated contexts; you can tune TTLs. It helps when you have repeated queries — reduces compute. Also we recommend quantized weights for lower cost. We'll show example profiles in the sizing sheet.
02:34 Priya Desai: For the quickstart, how many tokens of promo do you usually give? We want to get engineering to spike this within the week.
:02:42 Ellen Park: We generally grant 5-15k tokens for PLG quickstarts; for a POC we can do 10k today, I'll confirm in an email. That should be plenty to run a few end-to-end tests and measure latency.
03:00 Miguel Santos: What does the quickstart look like? Steps?
03:06 Marcus Li: Step 1: sign up and get API key in console. Step 2: pip install redwood-sdk (or npm), copy sample request — usually a 3-line curl to hit /v1/generate with model param. Step 3: run 1-2 sample prompts, check latency and token counts. We provide an example script that logs latency and headers so you can see how routing/fallback behaves.
03:28 Priya Desai: Routing/fallback — you mean when a model is overloaded?
03:32 Marcus Li: Right. For hosted we do smart routing across regions and model variants; for Dedicated you get reserved GPU pools and autoscaling. We also support an automatic fallback policy to cheaper model variants if latency budgets are breached.
03:45 Leah Kim: Do you have SOC2 or ISO artifacts we can share with auditors? They ask for evidence on encryption in transit and at rest, key management, and access logs.
03:53 Ellen Park: Yes, we have SOC 2 Type II and an ISO snapshot. We'll pull the redacted report and share via secure link. For Private deployments you can keep logs in your own storage to satisfy auditors.
04:08 Priya Desai: Good. Timeline — we'd like to have a working prototype by end of next week if possible. Is that realistic?
04:14 Ellen Park: Totally reasonable. If you sign up today and run the quickstart we should see a first-token test within the hour; end-to-end prototype within a couple of days assuming you allocate a couple engineers.
04:23 Miguel Santos: Any gotchas for latency — cold starts, long seq lengths?
04:28 Marcus Li: Cold starts can matter if you're using new model variants or very large context lengths. Our runtime optimizes kernel selection and KV cache warms with repeated prefixes. For short prompts under ~256 tokens you should see consistent sub-500ms latency on a decent instance. If you need <200ms at scale, Dedicated with optimized batching and smaller quantized model variants is the path.
04:48 Priya Desai: For compliance and data residency, could we choose a specific region? We need EU-only for some customers.
04:54 Ellen Park: Absolutely — we can pin regions. Hosted supports region selection for most models; Dedicated/Private you'll control region and infra.
05:02 Leah Kim: SSO — do you support SAML/Okta?
05:05 Ellen Park: Yes SAML/Okta, SCIM provisioning, and we support RBAC roles via the console. We'll include SSO setup notes.
05:12 Priya Desai: How about rate limits and quotas during prototyping — will the demo account be throttled?
05:18 Ellen Park: Quickstart credits come with elevated but limited quotas to avoid abuse. We can temporarily increase quotas for POC if you let us know the expected QPS.
05:27 Miguel Santos: One more: how invasive is the Dedicated setup? I.e., how long to get a dedicated pool up and running and latency guarantees?
05:33 Marcus Li: With provisioning it can be days to weeks depending on commit level and hardware. We have prebuilt Dedicated configs — typical time-to-prod for Dedicated is 2-4 weeks including security reviews. For immediate evals hosted is quickest.
05:47 Priya Desai: For our execs, a simple ROI: if we get reduced reconciliation costs by automating 40% of manual work, we need predictable unit costs. Can you provide estimate templates?
05:58 Ellen Park: Yes we'll send the cost/throughput template. It has fields for tokens/day, seq length, expected QPS, and shows hosted vs committed dedicated cost per month.
06:10 Miguel Santos: Can you also include an example of canary rollout and automatic fallback? We want to see how chaos/failover looks.
06:17 Marcus Li: We'll include an example policy — canary with 10% traffic for 24 hours, metric-based rollback on latency/p95 or quality regression. We also have hooks for evaluation to compare outputs.
06:30 Priya Desai: Speaking of quality, do you support eval harnesses?
06:34 Ellen Park: Our Optimize product can run prompt set evaluations and trigger regression alerts. For a POC we'll usually recommend a small eval set to detect quality drift when you switch model variants.
06:44 Miguel Santos: Ok so next steps: we want the quickstart assets and credits, your preliminary sizing sheet, and an intro to a security contact. Also schedule the deeper technical sync.
06:54 Ellen Park: Sounds good. I'll send the quickstart deck and credits. Marcus will assemble a sizing spreadsheet and sample dedicated config. We'll also include the security pack and a redacted SOC2.
07:03 Leah Kim: One question about logs — retention policy for hosted — can we reduce retention to 30 days or ephemeral? Some of our data is PII.
07:12 Ellen Park: Yes retention is configurable; for PII routes we recommend no-log ingest or redaction at the edge. For Private you can retain logs in your own S3.
07:22 Priya Desai: When you say "first token in 2-5 minutes" — what's the practical path?
07:26 Marcus Li: Sign up, open console, create API key (~1-2 min). pip install redwood-sdk (30s-2min). Run curl sample — first request hits and returns prompt token. If you run their script with logging you get latency metrics immediately. So if the team sits with it, many hit first token inside five minutes.
07:45 Miguel Santos: Are there any SDK compatibility issues? We're on Python 3.9 and Node 18.
07:50 Marcus Li: Supported — Python 3.8+; Node 14+. We'll include a sample repo.
07:58 Priya Desai: Great. Are there any legal or procurement items to flag early? We have standard DPAs and need to understand data processing terms and liability caps.
08:07 Ellen Park: Procurement typically gets our standard enterprise terms; for POC there's a simple TOS. For enterprise Dedicated/Private we'll engage legal and can start the procurement dialogue in parallel to the technical POC.
08:20 Leah Kim: Can you confirm which parts of the stack would be auditable for us — e.g., access logs, admin actions, model version history?
08:28 Marcus Li: Yes access logs and admin audit logs are available. Model versioning history and rollout events are stored and you can export them. We'll show what the console exports look like.
08:40 Priya Desai: Ok I think we have what we need to move forward. Quick question on fallback — how likely is quality drop if you switch to a cheaper variant?
08:47 Marcus Li: Depends on model gap and prompt sensitivity — that's what the eval set is for. We can help pick candidate cheaper variants and measure BLEU-like metrics or task-specific scoring. We'll flag possible regressions before rolling to 100%.
08:59 Miguel Santos: Any required firewall rules for Private? We'll need ports and endpoints.
09:04 Marcus Li: We'll send a network checklist; generally you need outbound/inbound to the runtime endpoints, mTLS certs, and S3 endpoints if you use managed storage.
09:15 Ellen Park: Alright last bit — I'll summarize actions in the follow-up email and include the quickstart link. Expected deliverables: quickstart deck + 10k credits, sizing sheet, security pack, and a proposed time for the deep technical sync.
09:29 Priya Desai: Thanks, look forward to receiving items.
09:33 Ellen Park: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up.
09:37 [call ends]
